study.title: Acts 5 - Holiness, power and perseverance of the church
study.overview: Acts 5 shows two parallel movements: the seriousness of God in the face of hypocrisy within the Christian community and the expansion of the gospel despite external opposition. The chapter begins with the case of Ananias and Sapphre, in which the lie is not only against people, but against God, bringing judgment and fear over the church. Then the narrative highlights signs, healings and growth, while religious leaders react with envy, arrest the apostles and then see them freed by divine intervention. In the judgment before the council, Peter states that it is necessary to obey God above the people and witness that Jesus was raised and exalted. The chapter ends with the prudence of Gamaliel, the flogging of the apostles and their persevering joy in continuing to teach Jesus daily in the temple and in the houses.

outline.title: The hypocrisy of Ananias and Sapphrerah and the holy fear
outline.explanation: Ananias and Sapphire sell a property, but hide part of the value while simulating total generosity. Peter denounces that the lie is against the Holy Spirit and therefore against God. Immediate judgment on the two produces great fear throughout the church and in all who hear.

outline.title: Signs, unity and church growth
outline.explanation: The apostles operate many signs and wonders, the people esteem, and more believers are added to the Lord. The text also shows the intense expectation around Peter's ministry, with sick people being brought in to be healed, including those tormented by unclean spirits.

outline.title: Prison, liberation and testimony before the council
outline.explanation: Taken of envy, the high priest and the Sadducees arrest the apostles, but an angel frees them and sends them to continue proclaiming the words of this life. Revealed in the temple, Peter and the rest claim that they must obey God before the people, proclaiming the resurrection and exaltation of Jesus as Prince and Savior.

outline.title: The council hesitates and the mission continues
outline.explanation: The council wants to kill the apostles, but Gamaliel advises prudence and recalls that merely human works end up for themselves. The apostles are flogged and forbidden to speak, but they come out joyful for suffering by the name of Jesus and continue teaching and proclaiming Christ daily.

study.context: The chapter depicts the life of the church in Jerusalem amid internal and external pressure. Within the community, Ananias' lie and Sapphira threatens the integrity of the body of believers; outside it, religious authorities resist the apostolic message. The text mentions the temple, Solomon's porch, public prison and supreme council, showing that preaching took place in public space and under strong scrutiny. The notes also mention Sadducees, Pharisees and Gamaliel, without expanding beyond what the chapter presents.
study.theology: Acts 5 teaches that God takes the holiness of his people and the truth before him seriously. Ananias and Sapphra's lie reveals that false religious appearance can be judged severely when it destroys the integrity of the church. At the same time, the chapter shows that the gospel advances by divine power, not by human force: signs, deliveries and growth accompany mission. The center of apostolic preaching is the resurrection of Jesus, his exaltation by God as Prince and Savior, and repentance and forgiveness offered through him. It also stands out the obedience superior to God: when human authorities forbid testimony, the apostles understand that they must continue to proclaim Christ. Suffering because of Jesus" name is not a sign of defeat, but it can be a cause for joy and fidelity.

scholarViews.insight: Ananias' lie was not only against people, but against the Holy Spirit; therefore discipline reached the very basis of sincerity and integrity of the church.
The chapter shows that after the judgment on the hypocrites, the gospel continues to advance with many signs and wonders, demonstrating the power of God in the midst of the opposition.
The apostles do not cease to teach and preach Jesus daily, taking advantage of public meetings in the temple and the particular opportunities to proclaim the Christian faith.

questions: What in my service to God can be external appearance without real sincerity before him?
When I am pressured to keep silent, am I willing to obey God above human approval?
Does my reaction to suffering because of Christ look more like discouragement or joy and perseverance?
study.practice: Examine your motivation when serving: God is not impressed with the appearance of generosity, but with truth and whole heart. Confess any duplicity, seek integrity in words and offerings, and continue to witness to Christ with courage, even when there is opposition. In practice, set aside daily time to speak of Jesus in public and domestic environments, with reverence, clarity and joy.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided do not base the historical location of some events accurately or to develop details about dates, geography or the context of Teudas and Judas beyond what has already been mentioned by the commentators. It is also not possible to affirm, from this material, as exactly the episode of Ananias and Sapphire relates to the whole ecclesial discipline in a broad sense; this remains an interpretative reading.
